graph.summary: Cytochrome P450 2C19 (CYP2C19) → Clopidogrel → P2Y purinoceptor 12 (P2Y12 receptor) → platelet aggregation → blood coagulation → Stroke

evidence.snippet: The CYP2C19 enzyme metabolizes clopidogrel, a prodrug, to its active form.
evidence.explanation: CYP2C19 activates the clopidogrel prodrug to its active metabolite.

paper.title: Genetic Determinants of Response to P2Y12 Inhibitors and Clinical Implications.

evidence.snippet: Clopidogrel is an antithrombotic prodrug, whose active metabolite inhibits platelet function by irreversibly binding to the platelet receptor for adenosine diphosphate, P2Y(12).
evidence.explanation: The active metabolite of clopidogrel irreversibly binds and inhibits the P2Y12 ADP receptor.

paper.title: Response variability to clopidogrel: is tailored treatment, based on laboratory testing, the right solution?
paper.journal: Journal of thrombosis and haemostasis : JTH

evidence.snippet: A key component of thrombotic events is the activation and aggregation of platelets, of which the P2Y1 and P2Y12 receptors play a crucial role in this process.
evidence.explanation: The P2Y12 receptor mediates platelet aggregation.

paper.title: P2Y1 and P2Y12 Receptors Mediate Aggregation of Dog and Cat Platelets: A Comparison to Human Platelets.

evidence.snippet: its surface membrane protein GPIIb/IIIa receptors activate platelets through fibrinogen to form platelet-platelet aggregates, and further activation of active substances such as ADP and TXA2 released by platelet alpha particles, which contribute to the formation of irreversible platelet aggregation.
evidence.explanation: Platelet aggregation drives thrombus formation and coagulation.

paper.title: Effect of pathological high shear exposure time on platelet activation and aggregation.

evidence.snippet: cerebellar ischemic lesions secondary to thrombus formation in dolichoectatic basilar artery.
evidence.explanation: Thrombus formation causes ischemic stroke lesions.

paper.title: Bilateral Internal Carotid Artery Agenesis and Posterior Circulation Stroke: A Rare Association.
paper.journal: Journal of stroke and cerebrovascular diseases : the official journal of National Stroke Association
